local.title: Snow rules for **Flint businesses.**
local.intro: Flint's colleges, hospitals, downtown offices along Saginaw Street, churches and apartment buildings all follow the same snow rules, and those rules shape how a lot gets cleared.

points.title: Walks are the owner's job
points.body: The city has said clearing sidewalks is the property owner's job under its ordinance. For a business that means the public walk along the frontage, plus the walks, ramps and steps to every door.

points.title: No piles in the street
points.body: Snow from lots and drives cannot go into the street. The city asks businesses not to push it there, and Michigan law bars depositing snow on a roadway or piling it where it blocks a driver's view. We plan where the piles go before the first storm.

points.title: Downtown is plowed early
points.body: The city's snow plan treats downtown as its own area and plows it overnight or in the early morning, before parked cars and traffic. A downtown entrance and walk are best planned around the same schedule.

points.title: Some big roads are the county's
points.body: Dort Highway, Corunna Road and parts of Court Street and Ballenger Highway are Genesee County Road Commission roads inside the city. If your entrance is on one, the county's plow, not the city's, sets when the ridge shows up across it.

logistics.title: How a commercial account starts in Flint.
body: Rob walks the lot with you or your manager before winter: entrances, drive lanes, walks, steps, where snow can be stacked and where it cannot. Then he explains the commercial snow and salting package options and quotes the property.

During a storm our trucks plow the lot and the drives, walks get cleared to the concrete, and ice melt goes down at entrances, ramps and steps. Snow gets stacked on the property, away from the sight lines at the exits.
In summer we mow, trim, edge and blow off the grounds, keep the beds weeded and mulched, and handle the spring and fall cleanups. We are licensed and insured, and you have one person to call.

faq.q: Do you do commercial snow removal in Flint?
faq.a: Yes. Grand Scapes plows and salts parking lots, drives and walks for businesses, churches, offices and property managers in Flint, with our own trucks. Estimates are free.

faq.q: Who has to clear the public sidewalk in front of a business in Flint?
faq.a: The property owner. The city has said sidewalk clearing by owners is required by ordinance, and it asks businesses not to push snow into the street. Check with the city for the current rule. Clearing the frontage walk can be part of your service.

faq.q: Where does the snow from a parking lot go?
faq.a: On the property. Michigan law bars depositing snow on a roadway and piling it so it blocks a driver's view at the road, so piles go to the back or the sides of the lot, away from entrances and walks.

faq.q: Do you mow and maintain commercial grounds in Flint too?
faq.a: Yes. We mow, trim, edge and blow off commercial grounds weekly, keep the beds clean and mulched, and do spring and fall cleanups. See [commercial grounds and snow](/commercial/) for how a year-round account works.

faq.q: Can you handle an HOA or an apartment property?
faq.a: Yes. We plow and mow for associations and rental properties as well as businesses. The board or the manager gets one contact, Rob, for the walk-through, the quote and any questions during the season.
